title: AI governance plane
tagline: One gateway, one budget ledger, one release gate for every AI workload in the company.
summary: A shared platform sits in front of all model traffic. Product teams get approved models, keys and budgets through a portal; every call is routed, cached, scanned and attributed; releases pass an evaluation gate; finance sees cost per workload and per accepted result.
customer_job: Let twenty product teams ship AI features fast while the company can answer what each one costs, which data it sends where, and whether it got worse.
baseline: Each team holds its own provider keys; spend appears as one invoice line; nobody can stop a regressed prompt before customers see it.
accepted_result: A workload release that passed its evaluation gate, with its traffic attributed and inside its budget.

primary_metric.name: Governed share of model traffic
primary_metric.definition: Model calls routed through the plane with workload attribution, divided by all model calls observed on provider invoices.

economics.basis: Illustrative assumption: tasks are workload releases per month; minutes saved are setup and review time per release. Model spend savings from caching and routing are a separate measured ledger.

flows.label: Approval for new model or data class

journey.title: Register a workload
journey.narration: A team registers its workload, data class and budget. It receives a key bound to that workload; provider keys stay in the plane.

journey.title: Approve what is new
journey.narration: A new model, region or data class goes to the review board once; approved choices become policy, not tickets.

journey.title: Route every call
journey.narration: Calls pass guardrails, policy lookup and routing with fallback. The gateway holds the provider credential.

journey.title: Attribute every cent
journey.narration: Each call lands in the cost lake with its workload tag; dashboards show cost per accepted result, not only per token.

journey.title: Block regressions before customers see them
journey.narration: Pipelines run the workload's eval suite before promotion. A regression blocks the deploy and shows the failing cases.

team.step: Product team registers, ships, reads its cost and eval results

evals.name: Governed traffic share
evals.threshold: >= 0.95 of invoiced model spend traced to a workload
evals.method: Monthly reconciliation of the lake against provider invoices.

evals.name: Gate coverage
evals.threshold: 100 percent of production AI releases ran the gate

risks.control: Provider keys exist only in the plane; egress rules; invoice reconciliation.

risks.risk: Gateway outage stops all AI features.
risks.control: Multi-region deployment, fail-open policy per workload class, tested runbook.
Report cost per accepted result beside spend; provider consumption is a separate ledger.

gcp.headline: Apigee as AI gateway with Model Armor and BigQuery chargeback
gcp.notes: Apigee policies enforce token quotas and routing; Model Armor screens prompts and responses; BigQuery holds the call lake for Looker Studio chargeback.
gcp.rationale: Enterprise-grade controls; Apigee configuration is a skill the platform team must hold.

vercel.headline: AI Gateway with budgets, BYOK and observability
vercel.notes: AI Gateway already provides one key for many providers, fallbacks, BYOK and usage views; the plane adds workload registration and the release gate.
vercel.rationale: Fastest path for teams already on Vercel; enterprise data-residency and audit needs confirmation.

cloudflare.headline: AI Gateway with guardrails, unified billing and Logpush
cloudflare.notes: AI Gateway handles caching, rate limits, guardrails and unified billing across providers; logs flow to R2 for chargeback.
cloudflare.rationale: Strong edge control plane at low cost; release gating is application work.

aws.headline: Bedrock inference profiles, Guardrails and CUR-based chargeback
aws.notes: Application inference profiles tag cost per workload; Guardrails apply per profile; CUR feeds dashboards.
aws.rationale: Native attribution for Bedrock traffic; non-AWS models need a separate gateway.

azure.headline: API Management AI gateway with Content Safety and Cost Management
azure.notes: API Management token limits, semantic cache and load balancing across Foundry deployments are documented gateway capabilities.
azure.rationale: Mature pattern on Azure; tier choice drives cost.

railway.headline: Self-hosted gateway proxy with Postgres and Grafana
railway.notes: An open-source LLM proxy you operate gives routing and budgets; you own uptime, upgrades and security.
railway.rationale: Portable and cheap; operational risk sits with your team.
